title: bswf-world
label: The Clark

won.source: No title-change document survives. The Clark is first attested as champion already defending the belt on the fed's own Monday Mayhem broadcast — his own reign's start is inferred backward from that defense, precision unrecoverable.

lost.source: The fed's own served Monday Mayhem broadcast: The Clark loses the BSWF World Championship to Merchandi$e, Wrestletech's own interference (a "Clark Bottom" of his own, then the "TECHsas maple leaf") turning the match. No exact date survives on the document itself; the broadcast's own text places it before an approaching "new year," i.e. late 1999.

how: Holder unknown to have won the belt from Ceesalo by any surviving document; lost it to Merchandi$e at Monday Mayhem.
note: The transition from Ceesalo's own reign is unrecorded — The Clark's own reign is registered on the strength of his documented loss of the title, the only evidence the held record carries for it.

title: bswf-world
label: Merchandi$e

won.source: The fed's own served Monday Mayhem broadcast: Merchandi$e defeats The Clark for the BSWF World Championship, Wrestletech's own interference turning the match, "the groggy ref... counted the three count for, the first time BSWF world champion, now truly a made man, Merchandi$e." No exact date survives on the document itself; the broadcast's own text places it before an approaching "new year," i.e. late 1999.

how: Defeated The Clark for the BSWF World Championship at Monday Mayhem, with Wrestletech's own interference turning the match.
note: Still champion on the fed's own undated Rankings page (with Debo named #1 contender) and on the fed's own Thursday Night Thump-Fest broadcast, the held record's last-attested state of the title. At Thursday Night Thump-Fest, Debo carries off the physical belt from ringside during a post-match angle after chokeslamming Merchandi$e — "if he wanted his title back he knew where to find him" — a challenge, not a title change; no pinfall or official transfer is staged anywhere in the held record.

title: bswf-world
label: Ceesalo

won.source: The fed's own served "Super September" Pay Per View recap: Ceesalo defeats Nick Hart in the tournament final, "Your Winner and New BSWF world Champion CEESALO." No exact date survives on the document itself; the PPV's own name places it in September 1999.

lost.source: No title-change document survives for Ceesalo's own loss of the belt. His successor is now known (see bswf-world-r002) but the match where he lost it is not part of the held record.

how: Won the finals of a six-man title tournament; the belt's own founding reign in the held record.

title: bswf-tag
label: Made Men

won.source: No title-winning document survives. The Made Men (Merchandi$e and Mi$ta) are first and only attested as champions on the fed's own undated Rankings page.

how: Not recorded — the held record's last-attested holders, per an undated Rankings snapshot.
note: Defended, without a declared result, against Kadafi and Scarface at Thursday Night Thump-Fest — the referee is pulled from the match by the Made Men Body Guards before any count, and the fed's own text never rules a winner. The corpus records no further title change after this document.
